evidence: Source review against native build 1: existing Ticket, conversation, artifact, error, and update response shapes remain readable. The optional machine_id health query preserves the original executor response when omitted, as APIClient.executorHealth does today. Destination-specific health is available in the web interface; native build 1 still reads the original executor health and does not expose the new selection. Legacy vps/macos aliases remain for the original destinations. Machine credentials and protocol 26 protect executor routes, which the native APIClient does not call. Executor reads now check the dispatched URL path before any file route can run. Shared Ticket reads retain existing agent permissions. The original executor transition keeps one recoverable pending credential until its first authenticated request, then permanently closes old authority. This changes executor authentication rather than native owner authentication. The runtime connection pool preserves native database transactions and commit participants. The retained cache matches existing request-worker concurrency. Exhausted retained slots use temporary connections without a pool wait. Cleanup preserves the original operation error. Existing API response shapes and native owner authentication remain unchanged. The default health response retains _with_native_build_1_fields. The native build floor, draft/outbox code, reconnect paths, and APNs payload are unchanged. Focused source review, destination health HTTP coverage, and Svelte checks support retaining build 1 for its retained interface. Signed-device, TestFlight, native destination-specific UI, reconnect, and draft-survival behavior are not tested. This is a source compatibility receipt, not device or release readiness. Final source, migration, and native-context fixture checks retain their original assertions with machine ownership and foreign keys active.
